subject: [PulseGate] sudden throttling, high latency and 5xx spike — urgent
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena@pulsegate.health>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@pulsegate.health>, PulseGate Engineering <eng@pulsegate.health>
Date: 2026-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production — sudden throttles/503s starting 08:45 UTC

Hi Neha,

We're seeing a large spike in latency and 5xx/429 responses across our inference calls since ~08:45 UTC. Throughput dropped ~40% and many of our end-to-end requests are timing out. This is impacting our monitoring dashboards and customer-facing pages.

Attached is a short log snippet (request ids, timestamps) showing repeated 429s and a handful of 503s. This looks like an enforcement change on your side — no config change on our end. Please confirm receipt and escalate — renewal conversation is sensitive right now.

Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
PulseGate Health

Attachments: pulsegate_429_log_snippet.txt
From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@pulsegate.health>
Cc: monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production — sudden throttles/503s starting 08:45 UTC

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm escalating immediately.

Initial ask: can you paste two sample request IDs from the attached snippet (the earliest and latest) and confirm which model / route these hit? That will let us pin the tenant and routing path.

We've opened an incident (SUP-4127) and I've looped in Monica (Customer Success) and Karthik (AE). Marissa is on copy for exec visibility.

Actions I'm requesting right now from infra: 1) hold any automated rate-limit policy changes for PulseGate tenant, 2) switch verbose request logging on for their tenant, 3) prepare an emergency quota override.

I'll come back with an ETA within 20 minutes after the first triage. Apologies — we know how disruptive this is.

— Neha
Head of Sales Ops (covering strategic accounts)
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production — sudden throttles/503s starting 08:45 UTC

Quick triage summary from infra/serving: we rolled a rate-limiter improvement on 2026-05-03 23:10 UTC that changed burst-credit replenishment semantics for the global quota controller. The change reduces short-term credit refill for tenants with sustained high concurrency to smooth out tail latency across all tenants.

For most customers this reduced token-level variance, but for PulseGate we're seeing their workload pattern (many concurrent medium-length streams + frequent replays) consume credits faster and hit the new burst floor. That interaction is producing repeated 429s and some downstream 503s as the serving runtime backpressures.

I've created a Jira (SUP-4127) and attached the relevant diff and a tenant quota snapshot.

Immediate recommended remediation:
- Roll back the burst replenishment delta for PulseGate's tenant to the previous profile (pre-2026-05-03).
- Apply a temporary +25% quota headroom and remove the new smoothing policy for this tenant.
- Keep verbose logging and collect 20 minutes of golden trace to validate.

I'll start the rollback in 5 minutes if we have exec approval to proceed.

— Monica
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rate_limiter_change-20260503.diff; tenant_quota_profile-vs-current.json
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Production — sudden throttles/503s starting 08:45 UTC

Marissa — heads up. PulseGate is one of our top strategic accounts (renewal Q3, expansion in pilot). If we don't restore their baseline throughput quickly this moves from an operational incident to an executive risk.

Requesting: approval to do an emergency tenant rollback + temporary quota increase as Monica recommends. Also please confirm we are comfortable offering a commercial remediation (credit or pro-rated refund) depending on the post-mortem. I'll coordinate with finance and legal if needed.

Karthik
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T10:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Production — sudden throttles/503s starting 08:45 UTC

Call to action (executive / engineering):
1) Marissa — please approve emergency rollback and temporary quota headroom for PulseGate (as Monica outlined). We need this authorized so infra can apply tenant-level override immediately.
2) Jonas (serving infra) — prioritize SUP-4127 on patch/rollback path and share ETA for when the rollback will be live. Rollback should be safe config revert (no binary change).
3) Monica/Karthik — continue customer comms: confirm ETA with PulseGate and offer a goodwill credit; don't finalize amount until post-mortem.

Planned timeline if approved now: 10:35 — apply tenant override and rollback; 10:40 — validate traces; 10:50 — update PulseGate and execs.

I'll standby on the incident bridge and join any quick sync.

— Neha
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Re: FW: Production — sudden throttles/503s starting 08:45 UTC

Approved. Jonas — execute the rollback and apply the +25% tenant headroom now. Keep me posted every 15 minutes until the service is stable.

After stabilization we need:
- A post-mortem that covers why the change didn't gate by canary for high-throughput tenants, the decision logic in the quota controller, and a mitigation plan to avoid tenant-level regressions.
- A proposed compensation package for PulseGate (Karthik: propose options and impacts; coordinate with Finance).

Thanks all — prioritize this over other lower-risk work for the afternoon.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
